claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Intrinsic atomic-scale lattice distortions govern the alloy's plastic strain and toughness.
Chemical heterogeneity in WTaTiVZr produces atomic-scale lattice distortions.
The lattice distortions create distributed local stress fields.
The distributed local stress fields facilitate simultaneous and spatially uniform dislocation nucleation.
The distributed local stress fields facilitate dislocation mobility.
Distributed dislocation activity reduces localized dislocation pile-up.
Reduced dislocation pile-up permits more uniform plastic deformation.
More uniform plastic deformation delays crack initiation and failure.
Time-dependent deformation in TaTiVWZr is dislocation dominated, as indicated by its creep stress exponent and activation volume.
Increasing temperature promotes thermally activated dislocation behavior in TaTiVWZr.
Prior refractory-HEA studies report distinct creep stress exponents and activation volumes associated with dislocation-mediated deformation.
Direct quantitative comparisons of dislocation nucleation and spatial distribution between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten remain largely unreported.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher strain-to-failure than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater strain hardening and a more uniform dislocation distribution than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is expected to dominate above 800°C but may be limited at lower temperatures or when irradiation substantially alters alloy chemistry.
